Pydantic models can have fields with aliases.

If a model has a field named `$ref`, Pydantic's `model_json_schema()` will include it in the `properties` of the schema.

from rich.text import Text

def test_strip_private_escape_sequences():
    decoder = AnsiDecoder()
    # \x1b7 and \x1b8 are private escape sequences for saving/restoring cursor position
    # \x1b0 is also a private escape sequence
    ansi_text = "Hello\x1b7World\x1b8!"

    # However, AnsiDecoder.decode returns an iterable of Text objects.
    # Let's use Text.from_ansi which uses AnsiDecoder internally.
    text = Text.from_ansi(ansi_text)

    ansi_text_0 = "Hello\x1b0World"
    text_0 = Text.from_ansi(ansi_text_0)
    assert str(text_0) == "HelloWorld"

    ansi_text = "Hello\x1b[31mRed\x1b[mWorld"
    text = Text.from_ansi(ansi_text)

from rich.markup import escape, render

def test_trailing_backslash():
    # If we escape "hello\", we expect it to be safe to use in markup.
    # If it's "hello\", and we append "[bold]world[/bold]", 
    # the trailing backslash might escape the '['.

    rendered = render(markup)
    print(f"Rendered: {repr(rendered)}")

    # render("hello\[bold]world[/bold]") will treat \[ as a literal [
    # and the result will be "hello[bold]world[/bold]" (with [bold] as literal)
    # But we wanted "hello\" followed by bold "world".
